html:
The steep stepped pyramid on the Great Plaza of Tikal, in the rainforest of northern Guatemala, built about 732 as the tomb of the king Jasaw Chan K'awiil I. It is the best-known building of the Maya.

It rises 47 metres in nine steep tiers, with one stair up the front to a small temple of three rooms. On top of that sits a tall crest of stone, called a roof comb, once carved and painted with a seated king. The king's tomb lay under the base, with jade, shells, pearls and bones carved with scenes of gods in canoes.

Jasaw Chan K'awiil had restored Tikal after more than a century of defeat, beating its great rival Calakmul in 695. The temple faces Temple II across the plaza, built for his wife. Tikal was left empty in the 800s, and the forest covered it until the 1800s.
sum: The steep stepped pyramid on the Great Plaza of Tikal, in the rainforest of northern Guatemala, built about 732 as the tomb of the king Jasaw Chan K'awiil I. It is the best-known building of the Maya.
